spreads.text: Nora drew four empty boxes in her notebook. "One is for a blue butterfly," she said. "The other three can surprise me." Mama and little cousin Jo came too.
spreads.visualAction: At the doorstep, Nora shows four boxes while Mama helps Jo with a tiny backpack.
spreads.characterState: Nora is expectant and ready to lead.

spreads.text: Along the garden path, Nora looked high and low. Red flower, yellow flower, white flower—but no blue butterfly. Can you point to something blue?
spreads.visualAction: Nora scans three colored flowers; a small blue garden object invites pointing.
spreads.characterState: Nora is focused on the expected prize.
spreads.pageTurn: A sudden sound breaks her concentration.

spreads.text: "BIRD!" shouted Jo. A sparrow fluttered from the fence. Nora frowned. "Now we'll never see anything." Jo's shoulders drooped.
spreads.visualAction: The sparrow lifts away as Nora frowns and Jo slumps.
spreads.characterState: Nora blames Jo; Jo feels shut out.
spreads.pageTurn: Mama makes room for both hopes.

spreads.text: Mama said, "You hoped for a butterfly. Jo hoped to help. That's two big hopes." Nora's tight hands opened a little.
spreads.visualAction: Mama kneels between the children; Nora uncurls her hands and glances at Jo.
spreads.characterState: Nora can reconsider without being shamed.
spreads.pageTurn: Nora needs a new way to look.

spreads.text: The garden path curved toward the creek. Mama whispered, "What can we notice without chasing or touching?" Nora made up a rule: "Eyes look, ears hear, gentle hands stay near."
spreads.storyFunction: causal location bridge, reframe, and refrain
spreads.visualAction: The same path visibly curves from the garden to the creek as Nora points to eyes, ears, and hands.
spreads.characterState: Nora invents a safe noticing method.
spreads.pageTurn: The new rule reveals a first surprise.

spreads.text: A silver snail slid across a wet stone. Its soft body rode beneath a hard shell. Slowly, slowly—a shiny trail appeared. Nora marked box one with a swirl.
spreads.visualAction: The family watches a snail from beside the path while Nora draws a swirl.
spreads.pageTurn: A tiny sound draws them onward.

spreads.text: Scritch-scratch came from a fallen log beside the stone. A pill bug curled into a tiny gray ball when the log trembled. Nora and Jo stepped back. Soon it uncurled. Box two got a dotty circle.
spreads.storyFunction: second discovery, explicit transition, and respectful distance
spreads.visualAction: The children step back from a curled pill bug beneath the nearby log.
spreads.characterState: Nora and Jo practice patience together.
spreads.pageTurn: Jo asks to join the game.

spreads.text: "My turn to notice?" Jo whispered. Nora remembered his droopy shoulders. She scooted over. "Your turn." Together they said, "Eyes look, ears hear, gentle hands stay near." Jo pointed—not too close—to three ants carrying crumbs.
spreads.visualAction: Nora makes room at the path edge while Jo points toward three ants.
spreads.characterState: Nora chooses kindness and includes Jo.

spreads.text: The ants followed one another toward a crack in the path. Nora drew three dashes in box three. "They found a way home," Jo said. Nora smiled at her noticing partner.
spreads.storyFunction: third discovery and natural consequence of inclusion
spreads.visualAction: Three ants trail to a crack as Nora shows Jo the matching marks.

spreads.text: One box was still empty. "What else can we notice?" Nora asked Jo. The sky turned from bright to dim. A cool puff brushed their cheeks. Leaves flipped their pale undersides.
spreads.storyFunction: renewed shared search and weather pressure
spreads.visualAction: Nora and Jo feel the wind and look up at dimming clouds and pale-backed leaves.
spreads.characterState: Nora seeks with Jo instead of hunting alone.

spreads.text: "Rain is coming!" Jo said. Plink! One drop landed inside box four. Plink-plink! Nora laughed. "The rain noticed my notebook!" They hurried home together—no butterfly, but four true surprises.
spreads.storyFunction: shared inference, payoff, and return trigger
spreads.visualAction: Jo recognizes the weather signs; raindrops spot the last box as all three turn home.
spreads.characterState: Nora celebrates Jo's noticing and the changed goal.
spreads.pageTurn: A quiet coda tests what changed.

spreads.text: By the window, Nora showed Jo every mark: one swirl, one circle, three dashes, and one raindrop. Then a blue butterfly crossed the garden—and kept flying. Nora smiled. "I noticed."
spreads.visualAction: Nora and Jo watch a blue butterfly through the window without pursuing it.
spreads.characterState: Nora can enjoy noticing without possessing or controlling.
